BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds

matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including

[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

loss amount.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft vs Buyer Playbook

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every risk-allocation point. Several positions are presented as "key negotiated" or "settled," but we have not agreed any of them. The Seller's 20% / AUD 4.8m cap is our conditional fallback, and no written authority from Amelia Frost exists, so we should not signal acceptance of it.

## 1. Clause-by-clause departures

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook position | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m opening; 20% only with Frost's written authority | Concedes our fallback without authority |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher; small claims excluded |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | 5x higher; first-dollar recovery removed |
| General time limit (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Frost approval) | Fallback used as opening |
| Limitation scope (12.3/13) | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated | Keep categories separate; no hidden override | Creates a general-regime override |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Title protection effectively removed |
| Limitations/reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of everything | No fraud carve-out at all |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public searches | Specific fair disclosure only | Deemed general disclosure rejected in our playbook |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | No claim for anything Buyer/advisers knew or could discover | Delete blanket exclusion; named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry | Sweeps in title, fraud and specific indemnities |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" | Effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion | Consent-on-delivery; endeavours insufficient |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Release "following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases | Post-completion release with no undertaking |
| DD-005 bonuses (funds flow) | AUD 420k excluded; "a matter for the Seller" | Specific line item or seller-funded, including triggered on-costs | Silent exclusion from funds flow; on-costs unaddressed |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity, preserve SOW3 cure | Narrow indemnity; SOW3 cure not preserved |
| DD-006 incident | "Not expected to be material" | Investigate, preserve logs, require updates; assume no confirmed breach | Materiality conclusion asserted by seller |
| Sandbar (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Characterisation accepted without assessment |
| Tax/IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Open; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed | Treated as closed |
| Title | Share register DD-012 is evidence of title | DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof | Seller's source treated as conclusive |

## 2. Reasoning on the material issues

**a) Caps, thresholds and time limits.** Taken together, the Seller's figures would cut recovery substantially. A AUD 250k basket with excess-only recovery means a buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of general claims. Combined with a AUD 25k de minimis, many individually small but collectively significant claims would be unrecoverable. The 18-month period is also short for a business with annual audit and tax cycles. These are fallback positions being offered as opening positions, and the 20% cap specifically would require Frost's written authority identifying the draft before we could accept it.

**b) Title and fundamental warranties.** Putting title and capacity under the general regime is the most serious structural departure. Title is a threshold question: if the Seller cannot deliver 100% of the shares, the Buyer has not bought the business. Title claims must sit outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar, with a 100% cap and at least six years. The seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale does not justify this. Its title evidence (DD-012) is also an internal register, not independent proof. We should require independent ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence (e.g., ASIC searches, PPSR, a Seller capacity certificate and board resolutions).

**c) Fraud carve-out.** The Seller's draft has no fraud carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature," which would extend the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language to fraud. Our playbook requires the carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive it. This is non-negotiable.

**d) Disclosure and buyer knowledge.** The combination of 1.1, 1.2, Sch 7 and 8.3 is a serious problem. The Seller would disclose everything in the data room and every public record, then bar claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge of" or could discover. Together these operate as a general disclosure of the whole data room with a knowledge bar on top. That would strip the Buyer of warranty protection for matters it has been told about in only the broadest terms. The disclosure letter is also brought down only to 5pm 22 September 2026, and it is now 6 November 2026, so we should require a bring-down.

**e) Bluefen and Riverlark (pre-Completion conditions).** Bluefen (about 30% of FY26 revenue) is a material customer consent. Treating it as "satisfied on delivery" and offering only reasonable endeavours removes the protection we need. We require an effective consent and evidence that its conditions (DD-002, clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion. The Seller's own disclosure confirms no final consent is in the data room. Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m outstanding) is similar: the Seller's disclosure says it has not been repaid and no discharge is included. We require a current payout figure, repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. A post-completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval, and neither is offered.

**f) Funds flow and bonuses.** The DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420k) are conditional, but the Seller's funds flow silently excludes them while describing them as "a matter for the Seller." Because the disclosure also says on-cost treatment (payroll tax, super) is unstated, the amount may be understated. The funds flow must either include them as a specific line item or make them seller-funded, including on-costs. We should not accept an unaddressed liability.

**g) Ironquay IP.** DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180k open, but this is not bank verification either way, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. The narrow indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and does not protect the transfer risk, so we should broaden it while preserving the SOW3 cure. We should not assert the AUD 180k is owed or that it has been paid.

**h) DD-006 export/privacy incident.** The Seller says the matter is "not expected to be material." The disclosure, however, says the investigation is preliminary, the scope is unknown, and there is no confirmed breach or notification determination. The playbook requires we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand. In practice that means: do not accept the Seller's immateriality conclusion; do not assert a breach either; and require log preservation, a completed investigation and regular updates. A specific indemnity for incident costs is worth raising with the deal team and Frost, though the playbook does not expressly require it.

**i) Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) and other supplier/lease/Mossvale items.** The Seller calls the Sandbar renewals "ordinary-course," but the disclosure says the timing and scope are unclear and they should be read together. We should assess them and avoid automatic Debt classification or a price deduction. Separately, DD-007 (lease notification) and DD-009 (Mossvale assignment) should be confirmed to not require consent merely because shares are sold. We should ask the Seller to confirm this in writing, not assume it.

**j) Tax and IP.** Calling these "settled under the general regime" is unacceptable. Tax and IP remain open. We should not assume unlimited liability or resolution, and they should be dealt with as separate categories, not folded into general warranties.

## 3. Recommendations (summary)

1. **Reject the Seller draft as the base document.** Issue our own mark-up from the playbook baseline (AUD 24m, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law).
2. **Do not accept the 20% / AUD 4.8m cap.** Our opening is 25% / AUD 6m. Any fallback needs Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Restore thresholds and time limits:** AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k first-dollar basket, 24-month general claims period.
4. **Separate Title/fundamental claims:** 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Require independent title evidence, not DD-012 alone.
5. **Insert a fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. No waiver.
6. **Reject general disclosure** (whole data room, public registers, Accounts). Require specific fair disclosure, and a bring-down to Completion.
7. **Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge bar** (8.3). Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must not excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
8. **Bluefen:** require effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours-only.
9. **Riverlark:** require a current payout and repayment from Completion funds. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
10. **DD-005 bonuses:** include AUD 420k plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line, or make them seller-funded.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. Do not assert the AUD 180k either way.
12. **DD-006:** preserve logs, require the investigation and updates, and reject the "not material" conclusion without asserting breach, harm or a numeric demand. Consider a specific indemnity (for deal team decision).
13. **Sandbar (AUD 330k):** assess; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
14. **Tax and IP:** keep open, separate from general warranties, with no assumed resolution or unlimited liability.
15. **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** Seller to confirm in writing that no consent is required for the share sale.

**Immediate actions for Amelia Frost:** approve or reject any cap, time-limit or disclosure fallback in writing, and decide on the DD-006 specific indemnity.
